statement: For the Alt–Burmester (5,0) equations, numerical continuation gives monodromy S4 on the four diagonal solutions and its induced action on the twelve ordered distinct pairs.

answer.text: Numerical monodromy computation gives S4, acting on the four diagonal solutions and on the twelve ordered distinct pairs.

group.description: S4 acting faithfully on the twelve ordered pairs (i,j), i != j, of four dyads; pairs ordered lexicographically. This is the off-diagonal component of the numerical Alt–Burmester computation.

source.version: Author draft dated 25 May 2016, corresponding to arXiv:1605.07806v1

notes:
The action is on ordered dyad solutions, not the quotient set of unlabeled linkages. No transfer of the full group to a restricted real parameter family is asserted.

Imported from the 2026-10-26 catalogue record R_0d6a1bb5e0daf37a; the source claim has not been newly rechecked against the paper for this beta import.

LMFDB link identifies the abstract group S4 (24.12), not its natural degree-four permutation action. The stored degree-twelve generators are induced by (1 2) and (1 2 3 4) on lexicographically ordered distinct pairs. They encode the described abstract action and do not certify the original numerical path tracking. The separate diagonal component has four points.

The fibre-product decomposition explains the diagonal and off-diagonal components. Loops around 64 branch points produce the displayed permutations. These are numerical path computations without exact path-tracking certificates.
scope: Alt–Burmester (5,0) problem in the isotropic-coordinate formulation of Brake et al.; dyads are ordered and prescribed poses/points general.
